decisions.reason: Moving the LEDs to the 3.3V rail does not change the DCDC1 output voltage, current rating, compensation behavior, or downstream rail target.
The AXP2101 remains the normal-operation power source and the system still requires both 3.3V and 5V rails; only the LED load assignment changes.
The existing message-444 MODIFY already removes the obsolete LED load and LED control attributes and narrows the 5V-rail contexts to sensor power.
Both 3.3V and 5V rails remain subject to current monitoring; changing which rail powers the LEDs does not alter the monitored-rail requirement.
The LED supply and data-interface decision does not affect the panel power-button connector, PWRON signal, or switching behavior.
The specified sensor-board connector matrix does not include the addressable LED power interface and remains unchanged.
The LED supply-voltage change does not modify ESP32 clocking, sleep policy, deep-sleep conditions, or wake sources.

Charge status remains displayed through the SK6812 chain, and the separate charge-status connector and resistor requirements remain unchanged; LED electrical supply is owned by the dedicated interface requirement.
The existing message-444 MODIFY already records the 3.3V supply, direct ESP32 drive, reduced threshold, removal of level-shifter parts, and accepted below-datasheet operating condition.
The LED rail decision does not affect the battery connector family, pin count, pin functions, mounting access, or unresolved pin order.
Battery overcharge, overdischarge, and thermal-protection requirements are unaffected by the LED supply-voltage change.
The project remains a three-board design and the main and sensor board roles are unchanged; the source only reallocates the LED electrical supply.
